verdicts.notes:
I checked all 12 r1 cards (6 true, 6 false). The balance is correct. Every source URL returned 200 and is official learn.microsoft.com (value-types, method-parameters, boxing-and-unboxing, reference-types, declarations, and the language specification pages for statements and variables).

Cards that passed, with the quote that settles each:
- 01 (value-types): \"In the case of value-type variables, you copy the corresponding type instances.\"
- 04 (method-parameters): \"The called method can't reassign the instance in the calling method ... when you reassign a parameter to a new value, that change isn't visible from the calling method, regardless of whether the type is a value type or a reference type.\" This also supports the explanation's mutation clause.
- 05 (boxing): \"Boxing a value type allocates an object instance on the heap and copies the value into the new object.\"
- 06 and 07 (boxing): \"Attempting to unbox null causes a NullReferenceException. Attempting to unbox a reference to an incompatible value type causes an InvalidCastException.\" Card 06 is right because (long) applied to an object holding an int is an unboxing conversion, not a numeric widening. Card 07 says \"a null object reference\", so it avoids the compile-time error that the literal (int)null would cause.
- 09 (reference-types): \"the equality operators == and != compare the values of string objects, not references.\"
- 10 (declarations): \"implicitly typed local variables are strongly typed.\" One nuance does not change the answer: in a nullable-enabled context var infers T? for reference types, but the type is still fixed at compile time from the initializer.
- 11 (spec 13.6.2.2): \"var z = null; // Error, null does not have a type\".
- 12 (spec 9.2): \"A local variable introduced by a local_variable_declaration ... is not automatically initialized and thus has no default value\". Also: \"The initial value of an instance variable of a class is the default value\".

Lesser observations, not flagged:
- Cards 01 and 03 rest on the same value-types sentence (assignment and argument passing both copy values). The prompt's scope lists them separately and neither answer gives away the other.
- Card 12 is close to definitional, because \"definite assignment\" names its own rule, but it is still an acceptable easy card.

Prompt rules: the pins hold. The C# 14 page says \"C# 14 is the latest C# release. C# 14 is supported on .NET 10.\" The C# 15 page says \"C# 15 is the latest C# preview release. .NET 11 preview versions support C# 15.\" The language-versioning page lists a .NET 10.x default of C# 14 and says \"C# 14 is supported only on .NET 10 and newer versions\".
